risks.risk: Wrong transmission type/spec (e.g., different bellhousing, gear ratios, or AWD/4WD vs 2WD) leading to non-fit or non-function.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the transmission ID/label/part number on the casing (and the mating bellhousing area) plus the vehicle drivetrain details (2WD/4WD, engine code).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used gearbox with unknown fit and unknown working status (worst case: not guaranteed to work / may require parts).

risks.risk: Missing components or damage not visible from this angle (solenoids, sensors, torque converter, harness connectors, linkage).
risks.proof: Photos of both ends of the gearbox (front/bellhousing and rear), all ports/connectors, and any loose/missing parts laid out.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/unknown condition until proven otherwise.

risks.risk: Internal failure risk (worn clutches/gears) despite being physically present.
risks.proof: Video of a functional test (bench test or installed test) showing engagement and no abnormal noises, plus fluid condition before/after.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working/untested until a test is provided.

risks.risk: Compatibility mismatch with the specific GMC Sierra years claimed (2008 vs 2014/2015 can differ by transmission generation).
risks.proof: Photo of the exact part number and/or a label that maps to the claimed years, or the donor vehicle details (VIN/engine/transmission code).
risks.if_unproven: Priced for the worst-case year mismatch (assume not guaranteed for the claimed fit).

proof_requests: Send a close-up photo of the transmission ID/label/part number on the casing (front and side) where it’s readable.
Send photos of the bellhousing/mating surface and the rear output area (ports/connectors) to confirm it’s complete.
Provide a short video of the gearbox being tested (or installed and shifting) and show fluid condition/leak check.
response.reason: The photo shows a gearbox assembly, but there’s no readable identification to confirm the exact model/spec or working condition, so a reliable worst-case price can’t be set without the decisive part number/test proof.
